entries.name: Buying and selling
entries.description: Exchange goods with a town using the company's finite cash account.
paragraphs: Buy moves goods from the public market into your ship or private warehouse and pays the town. Sell reverses those movements. A ship must actually be docked at that town; a remote quote is information, not permission to trade.

Choose a good and quantity, then read the exact order total before confirming. Manual trades execute the complete requested quantity or leave goods and cash unchanged. Quantity shortcuts only edit the proposal. Transactions do not advance the economic day.
Opening trade pauses playback. Close the window and resume deliberately when ready. Disable that ship's automation before issuing manual trades or sailing orders.

Harbor shows public market stock, the selected ship hold and local company stock together. Choose paid Buy/Sell for either accessible destination, or no-cash Load/Unload at the actual dock. Exact previews, quantity presets and specific blockers explain what can execute; a remote ship cannot move cargo here.

entries.name: Marginal prices and execution averages
entries.description: The displayed next price and the cost of a whole order answer different questions.
paragraphs: Ask is what you pay to buy; bid is what the market pays when you sell. In the regional scenario each unit changes public stock, so later units in a large order may have different prices.

The exact total adds the actual prices across the complete order. Average execution price is that total divided by quantity for display. Neither average nor the first marginal price replaces the exact total used for payment.

An automation price limit applies to the worst marginal unit in its selected order. A profitable-looking current quote does not guarantee the same price after a voyage, production, consumption, or another merchant's trade.

entries.name: Market liquidity
entries.description: Stock and money are separate finite limits.
paragraphs: A town can have goods to sell but too little cash to buy your cargo. Your company likewise needs actual cash to procure inputs, buy cargo, or construct a facility.
A blocked automated sale keeps unsold cargo aboard and explains the wait. Lowering a price limit cannot create buyer cash. Nothing silently replenishes stock or funds.

Classic and seeded v1 consumption removes goods without payment. Living Cities v2 households instead pay exact retail prices from their separate finite cash account; municipal Plank use remains an unpaid physical sink. Extraction creates goods, not money. Wages, retail, construction and trading transfer existing cash between named accounts.

entries.name: Cargo and storage capacity
entries.description: Every physical item uses one unit of ship or private storage capacity.
paragraphs: Capacity counts all commodities together. A hold containing several kinds of goods has less room for the next shipment even if the selected commodity's quantity is small.

Buying and transfers respect available stock and receiving capacity. Production checks the complete resulting private inventory before consuming inputs. A blocked batch does not partly consume materials.
Maximum trade quantities reflect current stock, exact payment, liquidity, and capacity. They remain previews and cannot authorize a remote transaction.

New v3 runs pool company storage per town. Capacity sums all granted and paid local facility warehouse capacities, including pending sites. Operational facilities with the same recipe add their output ceilings together. Pending sites provide storage but cannot produce early. Legacy saves keep their separate warehouses.

entries.name: Shipping and voyages
entries.description: Goods travel aboard a real ship between directly connected towns.
paragraphs: Departing changes the ship's voyage immediately without spending a day. Advancing economic days progresses travel. After arrival is committed, manual dockside actions are available at the destination.

Duration follows the route's distance and the ship's configured speed. Classic uses authored distances; seeded geography derives all six direct distances from the generated integer positions. Distances are abstract chart units, not coastline-aware sailing paths. Map drawing and playback speed never alter travel or economic calculations. You cannot trade or transfer while sailing.

There are currently no simulated ship-crew wages, fuel, voyage fees or transport losses. Living Cities models production wages only. Unmodeled transport expenditure is not a claim that shipping has no real economic cost.

entries.name: Company, market, and private ownership
entries.description: One company cash account supports distinct ship cargo and private warehouses.
paragraphs: A public market owns its stock. Buying from it changes ownership and moves cash. A factory's private stock belongs to its company and is separate from the town market, even when they occupy the same port.

Transfers between your ship and your warehouse preserve ownership and historical cost. They are not sales and move no cash or time. Both stores must have the same owner and the ship must be docked at the warehouse's town.
Remote management may buy or sell against a factory's local market. It cannot move goods to another port. Company cash shown beside a ship is the same account, not another balance.

Storage rules 2 give each company one town stockpile and one FIFO account shared by its local industries. Ships, public markets, other owners and other towns remain separate. Facility reports keep separate labor and production counters, never duplicate copies of the shared goods. Old saved runs retain storage rules 1 and their actual facility stores.

entries.name: Production and scheduling
entries.description: Complete canonical recipes run at explicitly scheduled economic days.
paragraphs: A recipe lists its actual input and output quantities. Transformation requires every input. Extraction has no tradeable inputs and creates its configured output. Canonical recipe pages describe quantities; the active scenario supplies intervals and limits.

A private factory consumes and produces only within its own storage. A successful batch schedules the next opportunity one interval later. Missing inputs, disabled production, or full output storage keep the batch due without accumulating catch-up batches.

Daily ship actions occur before procurement and production. Operational private procurement is followed by public production, private production, private sales, scheduled consumption, voyage progress and due construction completion. Fresh output cannot be loaded by an earlier ship action in that same daily operation. Pending factories skip their automatic phases even on completion day.

In Living Cities, a successful public batch pays the configured wage from market cash to local households; a private batch pays from its company. Insufficient payroll blocks the whole batch and keeps it due. Blocked, disabled, input-starved and pending batches pay nothing. After retail, city observations and population reviews occur before voyages and construction completion.

entries.name: Owning a factory
entries.description: Invest cash in a fixed recipe and a finite private stockpile.
paragraphs: The active scenario lists blueprints, eligible towns, construction payments, intervals and storage limits. Construction pays the local market once and creates empty owned storage. Ascension 0 is immediately operational; Ascension 1 new player sites complete after two economic days. The first batch is eligible one full production interval after completion, with inputs and capacity still required.

The industry summary shows status, next opportunity, missing inputs and local quotes, real expenditure and physical shipping waits. A recommended setup prepares a visible policy draft; only Apply commits it. Keep local output sales disabled, or retain an appropriate reserve, when a ship should transport finished goods. Detailed rules remain available.

A charter may grant an initial facility or goods. Those starter assets are grants, not purchases or construction payments during the run. Starter facilities are already operational at both ascensions and retain their initial schedule. Capital spending remains separate from material cost and sale margin.

Living Cities has town-specific construction eligibility. An industry may be absent and also impossible to build locally. Cash alone cannot override this restriction; use the eligible-town list and import missing inputs through real trades or shipping.

V3 makes Farms, Lumber Camps, Mills, Sawmills, Bakeries, Furniture Workshops and Silver Mines constructible somewhere, with eligibility visible before purchase. Multiple separate sites of the same eligible kind are allowed. A second Mill still needs Grain, paid labor, storage and customers; no construction creates free inputs. The public Royal Mint is commissioned separately and is never a private blueprint.

In new v3 runs a local Mill deposits Flour into the same owned town stock used by a Bakery. Facilities execute in stable port/ID order; an earlier eligible batch can consume scarce inputs before another. Only successful batches pay wages. Procurement targets and output reserves use current shared stock, so disable or reserve output sales when another local recipe needs it.

entries.name: Private procurement and local sales
entries.description: Maintain chosen inputs and sell chosen surplus through ordinary local trades.
paragraphs: For each recipe input, choose a target stock and maximum marginal buying price. A cash reserve protects company liquidity. Procurement buys only what the local town can supply and the company can afford within the policy.

For outputs, choose a retained quantity and minimum marginal selling price. Surplus sales use the town's actual cash and the same exact pricing as manual trades. Each configured good gets at most one transaction in its daily policy phase.

Targets compete for shared cash and warehouse space. A price, liquidity, stock, or capacity wait is a real constraint. Policies never discover a substitute source or create resources to meet a target. Under-construction sites do not automatically procure or sell until the day after completion; explicitly managing their local stock remains possible.

entries.name: Industrial shipping automation
entries.description: Connect owned production to physical transport and a chosen destination.
paragraphs: Choose a source market or owned warehouse, commodity, stock threshold, retained reserve, shipment target and minimum, destination, and selling limit. A route may deliver into an owned destination warehouse instead of selling. Optional return cargo can make the return voyage useful.

Warehouse loading removes your stock and adds it to the assigned ship without payment. Warehouse unloading reverses that movement. Market buying and selling use ordinary prices and finite cash. Every action requires the correct dock and ownership.

A route keeps an explicit outbound or return stage. It runs a bounded sequence of dockside actions and stops for travel, a wait, or incompatible cargo. Unsold cargo stays aboard; a blocked shipment is never discarded or teleported.

Read the current stage and wait reason before changing rules. Factory procurement, output reserves, and shipping must agree: a local sales policy can otherwise sell the stock that your ship was waiting to load. Automation executes your choices; it does not optimize a strategy or receive an economic bonus.

entries.name: Historical inventory cost
entries.description: Held goods carry actual acquisition or input-material expenditure through their journey.
paragraphs: Stock uses first-in, first-out acquisition lots in receipt order within each store and commodity. Several purchases at different prices remain distinguishable. A partial sale releases the earliest available slices at that store; transferred slices join the end of the destination queue with their original cost and provenance. Current market quotes never rewrite historical cost.

A lot's cost is allocated by exact cumulative integer shares. Taking a slice releases the difference between the cumulative shares at its end and start. Split transfers preserve that original interval, so slicing cannot manufacture or lose cost through rounding.

Production removes the historical material cost of its consumed inputs and allocates that total across actual output units in stable commodity order. Finished goods therefore carry their input-material cost. Transfers keep that cost without creating revenue.

Starter grants retain explicit grant provenance and zero purchased expenditure. That is not market value. Living Cities production wages are immediately expensed separately, not added to FIFO material basis. Depreciation, travel and other overhead remain unmodeled; zero material basis is not zero total economic cost.

entries.name: Financial reports and the ledger
entries.description: Separate cash, revenue, attributed costs, realized margin, and capital.
paragraphs: Sale revenue is actual money received. Cost of goods sold is the historical basis released by those sales. Realized gross margin is revenue minus that attributed cost. Unsold cargo and warehouse goods retain their basis instead of becoming realized profit.

Inventory purchases are cash outflows, while held inventory cost describes the purchased or manufactured goods still owned. Construction is separate capital spending, not another cargo purchase or a recurring charge on every manufactured unit.

The ledger identifies committed transactions, transfers, production, and grants with their company, store, commodity, quantity, time, and relevant cash or cost. The visible journal is bounded; authoritative lifetime summaries remain available after old detail entries leave the display.

Historical modes do not value ships and factories. Expanding Economy v3 adds a disclosed reference Company Value, not liquidation proceeds. Material gross margin remains revenue minus FIFO material cost. Living modes separately expense all actual wages: operating surplus after wages subtracts them, including wages for output still held. This is not full net profit after travel, depreciation, overhead or taxes.

entries.name: Starting company charters
entries.description: Choose one replacement starting package with understandable tradeoffs.
paragraphs: Run setup shows the selected charter's company cash, ship, cargo, facilities, and supplied stock. Merchant liquidity, an industrial foothold, and independent trading flexibility offer different opportunities rather than stacking upgrades.

Cash alone is not starting wealth. A granted factory or useful stock can support production while a larger hold changes shipping opportunities. Compare the whole package and the chosen objective before starting.

Starter assets are initialized explicitly and are not paid purchases during the run. The Industrial Consortium's inherited bakery is already operational even at Ascension 1, while newly purchased sites wait two days. This makes the modifier affect charters differently. A charter cannot change in an active run. Retry Same World restores its complete original run identity and assets.

entries.name: Challenges and run outcomes
entries.description: A challenge ends in victory, deadline defeat, or confirmed voluntary abandonment.
paragraphs: Run setup states the objective, deadline, and required cash. The supply charter counts signed net target-market sales minus purchases by your company. Buying back and reselling that market's goods cannot create delivery credit; merely arriving or transferring stock does not count.

Regional relief measures real scheduled consumption fulfilled in the configured towns. It is regional performance, not a claim that your company alone supplied every consumed item. An enterprise objective combines attributed financial performance with actual private production.

The complete economic operation finishes before the objective is evaluated. Success or deadline failure immediately freezes further economic actions. A victory acknowledgment offers View results while the frozen map, Journal and save remain inspectable. The final daily operation can succeed before the deadline failure check.

Sandbox has no victory deadline. An active run can be deliberately abandoned with confirmation. Explicit local saves preserve supported run modes; there is no cloud recovery or hidden automatic save. Retry Same World starts fresh rather than loading saved progress.

City Recovery in Living Cities measures six recent scheduled paid Bread opportunities at the vulnerable town. It requires at least 90 percent fulfillment against the greater of current and starting-population need, population at least its starting value, prosperity at least 55 and company cash at least 100 by day 90. Deliveries alone do not count; regional public/NPC contributions may help. A shrinking population cannot lower the baseline denominator.

Expanding Economy v3 offers the Grand Commission objective draft alongside separate provisioning, industrial-network and royal-commission objectives. Read the actual setup thresholds: paid welfare, real production, Company Value, liquid cash and monetary development are different requirements. Public Mint funding alone is not a victory or private company asset.

entries.name: Results and scoring
entries.description: Read the explicit score breakdown alongside the actual economy.
paragraphs: Results identify the challenge, charter, world mode, seed and generator version, ascension, outcome, completed day, objective progress, cash, actual revenue, attributed cost and margin, capital spending, factories, produced goods, deliveries, and remaining holdings.

Score combines four capped components: up to 500 objective points in proportion to completed progress; 1,000 points for victory; 10 points per remaining deadline day on victory, capped at 600; and one solvency point per 10 cash, capped at 100. Fractional points round down. Enterprise Ambition uses the lower of its production and margin progress for objective points. Total score cannot exceed 2,200; repeated transaction count earns no separate points. City Recovery objective progress is the lower of paid baseline-protected fulfillment and completion of its six-opportunity observation window; victory also checks population, prosperity and cash.

Compare results only within the same challenge, starting charter, ascension and exact world identity. Grand Commission identity also includes its draft version and exact selected objectives. Different seeds or selections are not equivalent leaderboard placements, and packages have different endowments. Retry Same World restores the original configuration; New World / Reroll changes the draft seed and previews it before a separate start.

Grand Commission objective points are floor(500 times the sum of its four card percentages divided by 400). A card uses its least-complete condition, with each bar capped from zero to 100. Victory still requires all four cards currently met and 100 company coins by day 180; partial points cannot award success. Permanent accomplishments and currently met conditions are distinguished in the Objectives Journal.

entries.name: Menus, pause, and the encyclopedia
entries.description: Inspect, pause, and begin another run without accidentally advancing the economy.
paragraphs: Start from the main menu, choose New Run or unlimited Sandbox, then review the challenge, charter, Classic, seeded v1, Living Cities v2 or Expanding Economy v3 preview, and Ascension 0 or 1. Setup, seed editing and reference browsing do not advance economic time or reroll a started world.

Escape first closes the active trade or industry overlay. From the encyclopedia it returns to the parent screen. During ordinary gameplay it opens pause; from pause it resumes unless a confirmation is active.

Restart, abandonment, return to menu, and exit protect unsaved active progress with confirmation. Exit closes the standalone game. Save explicitly before leaving; Continue or Load restores a valid local saved run, while Retry Same World creates its initial state again.

The encyclopedia is available from the main menu, run setup, and pause menu. Browse a category, search names or descriptions, follow related entries, and use Back to return. All recipe facts are generated from the same content the simulation loads and work offline. Settings offers four game-wide text sizes without changing the world.

New Run defaults to Expanding Economy v3 and the Grand Commission. Advanced / Legacy keeps earlier worlds accessible, and Sandbox remains explicit. Inspect the large interactive map before drafting; invalid seed text leaves the last valid preview intact. Retry and Load preserve the original run identity.

entries.name: Seeded worlds and exact retries
entries.description: Choose geography-only v1 or Living Cities v2 economic roles, then retry the exact run identity.
paragraphs: Fixed / Classic Archipelago retains the original map positions and authored sea distances. Seeded Archipelago moves the existing four towns, preserving their IDs, industries, markets, NPCs, initial goods and cash, ship speeds, demand and challenge deadlines. No seed receives secret assistance.

Enter an ASCII integer from -2147483648 through 2147483647, with an optional leading plus or minus and no spaces or separators. Generator version 1 uses a fixed integer algorithm with bounded slot placement and jitter. Its six direct distances derive from the same coordinates shown in the preview and map. Ordinary speed-100 ships take three to seven days per direct voyage.

Record the world mode, seed and generator version together with challenge, charter, ascension and Living Cities pricing hypothesis. That complete identity determines the initial run under current scenario definitions. Retry Same World restores original funds, stock, cargo, policies, facilities and clocks and clears the host journal. It does not preserve accumulated progress.

Randomize seed or New World / Reroll explicitly chooses a different draft seed in the host, previews it and waits for a separate start. Menus, encyclopedia and text settings cannot accidentally reroll. A valid navigable layout does not guarantee that any unchanged route policy will win.

Living Cities version 2 uses the same geography stream plus a separate bounded economy stream. Four authored role packages permute food supply, processing, forest furniture and vulnerable coast across the existing towns, with different population, cash, stocks and private capabilities. The forest furniture town has logging and furniture production but no Sawmill capability; it depends on imported Planks. Structural production paths do not guarantee perpetual solvency or victory.

Expanding Economy v3 reuses exactly the same seed geography and economic role permutation, while explicitly selecting fractional goods, new monetary rules, expandable industry and fleets. Content and reference-valuation versions belong to its identity. A v2 identity is never silently treated as v3.

entries.name: Ascension 1: Slow Foundations
entries.description: New player-owned factories need two complete economic days to become operational.
paragraphs: Select Ascension 0: Normal or Ascension 1: Slow Foundations before starting. Difficulty belongs to this run; it is not an unlock, prestige reward, stacking curse or permanent bonus. Ascension 0 preserves instant construction and the Classic baseline.

At Ascension 1, ordering a new player facility pays its full cost immediately and creates an under-construction site without advancing the day. Two successful AdvanceDay operations complete it. The site skips automatic procurement, production and sales throughout both days, including completion day's automatic phases.

A two-day bakery ordered on day 0 completes after day 2's voyage phase and first becomes eligible to produce on day 4. Its own stock, enabled state and capacity must still permit the batch. Completion grants no free inputs, does not charge again, and is recorded as a zero-cash event.

Manual local warehouse buying/selling, storage and physically docked owned transfers remain legal during construction under the normal cash, stock and capacity rules. They cannot produce early. Already-built starter facilities, including the Industrial Consortium bakery, retain their original schedule and grant provenance; later purchases still wait. This narrow industrial penalty need not affect every strategy equally.

entries.name: Text size and readable controls
entries.description: Choose one presentation scale for every ArchipelagoLab screen.
paragraphs: Settings offers Compact, Default, Large and Extra Large text throughout gameplay, map labels, trade, industry, automation, ledger, encyclopedia, setup, pause and results. Default body text is 17 pixels; Large and Extra Large use 21 and 25. Compact uses 14 for a deliberately denser presentation.

The primary sidebar groups Overview, Market and Controls into tabs and keeps ordinary actions separate. City Economy opens paused detail; industry advanced rules are collapsible. Panels wrap and scroll internally where text grows. Buttons, numeric fields and hit targets adjust with text rather than using paint-only zoom; long documents and advanced configuration intentionally retain scrolling.

Changing text size is passive: it does not advance time, change revision, spend cash, alter rules or reroll a seed. The text preference is remembered locally through Unity PlayerPrefs for the application environment, across menus and fresh runs. Other presentation settings last for the session. This does not save an economic run or synchronize preferences between devices.

entries.name: Living city accounts and wages
entries.description: Household money, market liquidity and company cash have separate owners.
paragraphs: Each living town has a public market account and an aggregate household account. Every company has one cash account. Living Cities v2 conserves their combined total after initialization. V3 additionally has a public treasury and finite external authority: external commerce transfers existing money across the regional boundary, and only an explicit Silver-backed Mint exchange creates new currency. There is no daily allowance or hidden stock repair.

A successful public production batch moves its wage from market to households. Private production moves its wage from the owning company to households. For example, a wage of 10 moves market 40 to 30 and household 20 to 30; no money is created.

If households then buy Bread for an exact order total of 18, household cash becomes 12 and market cash 48. Only the purchased Bread is consumed. Actual quantities use marginal price totals, stock and affordability; a first-unit quote multiplied by quantity is not the bill.

Market insolvency can block your sale even when households still have money. Retail may later fund the market only if food exists, households can afford it and a need is due. Buying locally, exports and private employment can move real funds; none guarantees a recovery day.

Open City Economy for separate cash balances, actual wage and retail payments, due needs, food failure causes and next opportunities. A missing item and an unaffordable stocked item are different constraints.

entries.name: Food, furniture and municipal use
entries.description: Different consumers need different goods on explicit schedules.
paragraphs: Bread is the essential household good, due every four days. Living Cities v2 rounds one Bread per 20 residents upward: population 20 needs one and 21 needs two. Expanding Economy v3 uses exact proportional quantities instead: population 10 needs 0.50, 15 needs 0.75, 20 needs 1.00, 21 needs 1.05 and 30 needs 1.50 Bread. Retail buys only actual affordable stock.

Essentials run before luxuries. Furniture is an infrequent durable household need: one per 80 residents every 24 days when sustained welfare enables it. V2 rounds upward; v3 is proportional with exact residual carry. Luxury spending reserves the exact current price of the next Bread need and cannot spend an unlimited future income.

Municipal Planks are a separate public own-use sink every 12 days. They move no cash to a fictional buyer. Grain, Flour and Logs are industrial inputs and traded goods, not household staples in this model.

Food coverage estimates physical stock divided by scheduled eligible household demand; it is not a guaranteed spending forecast. Goods without household demand show not applicable. Stock-only pricing remains the baseline. Experimental coverage pricing derives bounded stock targets from a seven-day need horizon constrained by actual household funds. Effective pricing parameters stay fixed until the next daily boundary; marginal bid/ask prices still respond to every inventory change.

entries.name: Population, prosperity and recovery
entries.description: Sustained paid food and purchasing power shape bounded city welfare.
paragraphs: Prosperity is a 0 to 100 indicator, not a cash or price multiplier. Up to six recent scheduled food opportunities, including failures to buy, supply a paid-fulfillment share. Current household cash is compared with a reserve benchmark for the next Bread need, priced exactly using current parameters and a hypothetical shelf containing at least that need. This is not a future availability or price promise. Three parts fulfillment and one part purchasing power set the target; prosperity moves toward it by at most three points per observation.

Furniture demand turns on after three consecutive qualifying observations with prosperity at least 65 and full food plus an affordable next-need reserve. It turns off after three consecutive observations with prosperity at most 40 or purchasing power below 25 percent. This hysteresis prevents daily threshold flicker; demand remains subject to real stock and budgets.

Population reviews occur every 12 days after six food observations. At most one resident is gained after sustained adequate food and prosperity at least 65, or lost after sustained severe deprivation and prosperity at most 35. Generated bounds are 10 to 80. New population changes subsequent desired need, not past records.

A city can keep household money yet decline because food is absent; another may have food but no purchasing power. Production inputs, payroll, market buying power and transport can all stall a chain. The model has no guaranteed long-run equilibrium. The City Recovery challenge tests sustained real recovery on a declared baseline, not a one-time shipment.

entries.name: Fractional goods and exact coins
entries.description: V3 households buy proportional quantities while ships carry whole cargo units.
paragraphs: Expanding Economy v3 stores 10,000 physical subunits per good and 10,000 monetary subunits per coin. Displays format those integers; they never change balances. Canonical recipes execute complete batches at this scale. For example, consuming 0.75 Bread from a shelf holding 2.00 leaves exactly 1.25.

A ship order must be a whole cargo-unit quantity. With 2.75 Bread for sale, a ship can load at most two whole Bread and leaves 0.75. Household purchases and local private storage can retain fractional stock. Capacity counts the actual combined goods once.

Exact totals sum marginal inventory edges. Splitting an uninterrupted order across fractional boundaries has the same total as buying the combined quantity, while every debit equals its credit. The displayed average is informational. Unrepresentable amounts fail rather than wrap or disappear.

An authored population fraction finer than one physical subunit carries its exact residual numerator to the next due opportunity. Food observations retain actual desired, purchased, stock-short and funds-short quantities. Current and initial-population need have separate carry, so population decline cannot erase the recovery baseline.

entries.name: Expanding production chains
entries.description: Invest in real capacity and inspect the next finite bottleneck.
paragraphs: Every v3 world permits all six original production building types somewhere. Eligibility follows economic roles, not displayed city names. The food source can host Farms; the processing town can host Mills and Sawmills. The forest-furniture town can host a Silver Mine but cannot build a Sawmill, preserving a real Plank import dependency.

Each owned facility has separate inventory, schedule, enabled state and policy. Multiple Mills may coexist. Public and private extraction create only their declared batch outputs, and every successful living batch pays its full configured wage from the real employer.

An extra Mill expands potential Flour output. Actual results still require Grain, wages and warehouse space, then a Bakery with Flour and Logs, and actual distribution to households able to pay. Overbuilding can consume cash without improving food access. Distinguish a recorded last-attempt failure from current conditions before changing policy.

entries.name: External trade and the public Royal Mint
entries.description: Finite outside purchases import cash; bounded Silver-backed issuance creates it.
paragraphs: The external authority has one visible finite account. A contract specifies goods, whole-unit quantity, harbor, payment and deadline. You must own and physically deliver its cargo there. Delivered goods leave the region; payment moves existing authority cash into the company. Completed quantities and spent funds never refill on expiry.

Exactly one processing-role harbor hosts the public Royal Mint. Commissioning pays the treasury once and starts its explicit construction delay. The institution belongs to the region and never counts as Company Value. The Silver Mine is in a different role, requiring real shipping.

An active ready Mint accepts one physically delivered Silver from the selected docked owned ship. That metal enters the public reserve and cannot be used twice. The authored batch creates 80 coins, paying 60 to the supplier and 20 to the treasury, with four days between batches and at most 24 batches. Silver material basis and Mint receipts remain separate from ordinary sale margin.

The treasury can buy a bounded real quantity of delivered Planks only while funded. Commission and minted public shares are actual treasury funds, not an unlimited credit line. Regional cash counts markets, households, companies and treasury. All-account cash also counts the outside authority. Only recorded Mint issuance increases all-account money.

Bread and Furniture purchases move existing household cash to markets and consume actual goods. Neither creates nor destroys coins. Extra money cannot replace missing Grain, Flour, Logs, employers or voyages.

entries.name: Commission and direct a fleet
entries.description: Up to three owned ships share cash but keep separate cargo and routes.
paragraphs: V3 permits the starting ship and two additional ships. The processing harbor shipwright charges 500 coins and consumes four real market Planks. Of that payment, 460 goes to the market and 40 to local households for labor. Construction takes four economic days; completion creates an empty ten-unit ship at that harbor.

Pending orders count toward the three-ship limit and retain paid capital in Company Value. Missing company cash or actual market Planks prevents the order without partial payment or a phantom ship. Private-factory Ascension timing is separate from this shipbuilding schedule.

Select the intended owned ship before trading, sailing, transfer or route editing. All ships share one company account, but each has its own cargo, position, policy, enabled state and industrial stage. Ships act in stable priority and ID order through one atomic day; one ship cannot load or spend another ship's cargo.

Configure complementary routes using the existing two-port policies. A useful return export can return money to an importing town. Automation still respects actual stock, household-independent market liquidity, price limits, company reserves and real voyages; it cannot discover a winning strategy for you.

entries.name: Company Value and operating results
entries.description: Reference holdings, liquidity and realized earnings are different measures.
paragraphs: V3 Company Value equals company cash plus reference value of every owned cargo and warehouse good, completed ships and factories, and paid pending ship or facility capital. Every store and asset appears once. Reference prices are stable authored values, not a promise that a finite local market will buy everything.

Starter goods and operational grants have positive reference value where appropriate but zero historical paid basis. FIFO paid basis is not added again to Company Value. Moving goods between owned stores neither creates value nor realizes a sale.

A ship is valued at 50 coins per whole capacity unit. Facilities use their authored replacement construction cost. A paid pending order is replaced by its completed asset at completion, without double counting. The public Mint, treasury, households and other companies are excluded.

Cash pays orders and wages now. Realized material margin is actual sale revenue less released FIFO material basis; operating surplus after wages also subtracts all paid wages, including wages for held output. Mint receipts, surrendered Silver basis and public commissions are shown separately. Company Value change is not realized profit or liquidation proceeds.

entries.name: Save, Continue and exact retry
entries.description: Local explicit saves preserve an economic run; retry starts its identity fresh.
paragraphs: Save explicitly to a local slot before leaving. Continue or Load restores a saved Classic, seeded-v1, Living Cities-v2 or Expanding Economy-v3 run without advancing its day. Saves are local to this installation; there is no cloud account or automatic cross-device recovery.

The save retains exact accounts, fractional stock and demand residuals, every ship and route stage, voyages, factories, pending construction, household history, FIFO lots, challenges and v3 contracts, Mint and treasury state. Grand Commission saves also retain the exact selected plan, per-ship visits and signed target-market history. Visual interpolation and focus are presentation state, while text size remains an independent local preference.

A load validates the complete file, identity, content and configuration before replacing the current session. Unsupported versions, damaged files, inconsistent stock or impossible states produce an error and preserve the valid active run. A saved terminal run remains frozen and inspectable.

Retry Same World always reconstructs the original initial identity and assets, even when a saved later state exists. Reroll explicitly chooses a new draft seed and requires preview/start. Neither action silently loads or overwrites your saved progress.

New pooled-stock v3 runs use save schema 3. Original schema 1/2 runs retain their old storage identity, format and behavior; loading never silently combines warehouses. Development builds and the Editor offer Export Run Report: an exact raw save plus a readable diagnostic under the displayed Exports paths. Export uses no save slot and changes no economic state; recent activity is partial bounded history.

entries.name: The Grand Commission and Objectives Journal
entries.description: Read the seeded map, draft four mandatory goals, and track real economic accomplishments.
paragraphs: Grand Commission is the default scored Expanding Economy v3 choice. Review all four towns, actual sea routes and building capabilities first. Then choose one of three distinct cards in each of four rounds: Navigation/Fleet, Production/Industry, Markets/Commerce and Civic/Capital. Each category has four real candidates. Backtracking preserves offers and never advances time. Review all four selections before Begin.

All four selected cards must be satisfied together by day 180, with at least 100 liquid company coins. Completed visits and actual production are permanent evidence; signed net sales, current facilities, cash, Company Value and recent paid-food conditions can become unmet. Each card shows its least-complete condition rather than hiding a blocker behind an average.

A New Industry needs an operational private Mill and Bakery in different towns, with a funded completed batch in each exact site. A starter Bakery beside the Mill does not satisfy the distinct-town condition. Pending construction, missing inputs, unfunded payroll, public output and purchased stock are not private production.

Destination commerce counts your company's actual sales minus purchases of the named good at the named town, for ship and private warehouse market trades. Buying four Flour and reselling those four locally earns zero; a later buyback can reverse imported delivery credit. NPC trades, quotes and unsold cargo do not count. Navigation records actual owned-ship docks and arrivals; a new second ship must sail beyond its shipyard to earn its second visit.

The navigation choices require four visited towns, three named role towns, a second ship visiting two towns, or three towns plus a positive remote net sale. Industry choices require distinct-town funded Mill/Bakery batches, a Lumber Camp/Sawmill with four private Planks, a Sawmill/Workshop with two private Furniture, or two-town Bakeries with four private Bread. Commerce requires four net Bread, Planks or Flour at the resolved destination, or 100 coins in finite external contract receipts.

Civic choices require a company-commissioned public Mint and one physical Silver issuance; recovery-town food coverage of 80 percent across six recent opportunities plus prosperity 50; Company Value growth of 100 coins with 100 cash; or two funded public-works Planks plus six recent food opportunities at 60 percent. Food uses actual paid consumption against the greater current and initial-population need. Deliveries alone are not meals, and welfare may fall again.

Open Objectives from play, pause or results for current/target quantities, completion bars and specific blockers. The map HUD keeps a compact currently-met count and days left. Journal inspection pauses playback. Permanent requirements are marked as completed; reversible requirements say currently met. Zero-clamped bars never erase a negative net balance.

Mission draft version 1 and its exact four resolved cards are part of run identity. The same seed keeps the same offers regardless of charter, pricing, Ascension or earlier choices, without changing the economic world. Save/Continue restores the current plan and progress exactly; Retry Same World starts that same commission fresh. Explicit reroll returns to a new preview. Older authored challenges, modes and valid saves remain available.
